papers.title: A TaqMan assay that knows its mite: specific detection of Tropilaelaps mercedesae Clade I
papers.authors: Marga P. E. van Gent‐Pelzer, Marc Hendriks, Terd Disayathanoowat, Patcharin Phokasem, Heather Graham
papers.abstract: Tropilaelaps mercedesae (Mesostigmata: Laelapidae), an invasive mite species native to South East Asia, is rapidly expanding its range, facilitated by global trade in bees and climate change. Recent detections in Eastern Europe raise concerns about its imminent spread into the European Union. As a notifiable parasite under the European Union Animal Health Law, member states are required to implement surveillance and prevent the spread to other member states. Rapid and reliable detection is critical to the success of such efforts. To support assay development, DNA was extracted from individual Tropilaelaps mites collected in Thailand, to generate species-specific genetic data. To validate the assay, synthetic double-stranded DNA fragments (gBlocks) representing target sequences were used as positive and negative controls, mimicking real-world DNA samples and confirming assay specificity. Here, we present a T. mercedesae Clade I specific TaqMan assay based on the cytochrome C oxidase subunit I gene, coupled with an efficient DNA extraction method from single mites, offering a sensitive molecular tool for early detection and monitoring.

papers.title: Predicting the potential habitat suitability of Phloeosinus aubei Perris in China using BIOMOD2
papers.authors: S. Ahmad, Xinqi Deng, Habib Ali, Quanfu Jiang, Zhihang Zhuo
papers.abstract: Abstract Phloeosinus aubei Perris, a bark beetle of increasing concern in China, poses significant threats to Cupressaceae species in both natural and managed landscapes. This study used 69 spatially thinned occurrence records and 10 environmental predictors with BIOMOD2 to predict its potential habitat suitability under current and future climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5). The ensemble model showed robust predictive performance (The Area Under Curve was 0.917, and the True Skill Statistic was 0.813). Variable importance analysis identified the minimum temperature of the coldest month (Bio6), mean diurnal range (Bio2), and human footprint as key drivers. Under current conditions, approximately 36.1% of China’s land area was suitable for P. aubei , with high suitability concentrated in the Yangtze River Basin, Sichuan Basin, and central-eastern provinces. Future projections indicate a 9–23% expansion of suitable habitat by the 2090s and a 350–500 km northeastward shift in the centroid of highly suitable habitat under high-emission scenarios. papers.title: Evolution of machine learning-based species distribution models: Technological development, research trends, and future challenges
papers.authors: Jinchen Xu, Gu Jiqi, Shufei Duan, Yanping Wang, Jie Xie
papers.abstract: Species distribution model (SDM) have become important tools for biodiversity assessment, ecological prediction, and conservation planning. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have expanded their capacity to analyse complex ecological data. However, the overall development trajectory, knowledge structure, and methodological implications of machine learning-based SDM (ML-SDM) remain insufficiently synthesized. This study provides a systematic overview of ML-SDM research from 2006 to 2025 by integrating bibliometric analysis with methodological synthesis. Using 5224 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, we combined bibliometric statistics, collaboration analysis, co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, temporal keyword evolution, and qualitative synthesis to investigate research trends, methodological development, knowledge accumulation, and future challenges. The results reveal rapid growth in ML-SDM research and extensive international collaboration, with the United States and China leading in publication output. papers.title: Evaluation of Gallery Injection for Management of Invasive Shothole Borers ( Euwallacea spp.) Associated with Fusarium Dieback in High-Value Trees
papers.authors: Beatriz E. Nobua-Behrmann, John N. Kabashima
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive shothole borers ( Euwallacea spp.)(ISHB) and their associated fungal pathogens cause substantial damage to urban and riparian trees, creating a need for diverse management approaches to accommodate different infestation scenarios. Gallery injection, a technique in which small volumes of pesticide are delivered directly into active beetle galleries, has not previously been evaluated for ISHB and may provide a localized treatment option that limits pesticide applications to infested portions of the host. The objective of this study was to evaluate gallery injection as a management approach for ISHB, compare the efficacy of different active ingredients delivered using this method, and quantify the volume of solution that could be delivered into active galleries under field conditions. Field trials were conducted on Platanus spp. in Southern California. Active galleries were verified prior to treatment, and beetle activity was assessed following injections. Gallery injections with emamectin benzoate and imidacloprid significantly reduced gallery activity relative to untreated controls, whereas acephate provided intermediate control. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. papers.abstract: Abstract The performance of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)-based biopesticides depends not only on their insecticidal proteins but also on the manufacturing process, from fermentation through downstream formulation. However, these stages are often investigated independently, limiting understanding of how process design influences the properties and performance of the final product. papers.title: ADVANCING BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION IN A RAPIDLY CHANGING WORLD: PLANT-CENTERED STRATEGIES FOR ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE, RESTORATION AND SUSTAINABLE FUTURE

papers.source: OpenAlex / SARPS Journal of Advanced Research in Plant Science
papers.abstract: Biodiversity conservation is shifting from the paradigm of species protection to the maintenance of ecological, genetic, and functional integrity. Earlier biodiversity research and conservation practice focused on understanding and responding to the drivers of biodiversity loss, e.g., habitat loss, climate change, environmental degradation, invasive species, and overexploitation. This review synthesizes the role of plants in sustaining ecosystems, with an emphasis on genetic conservation, ecological restoration, connectivity, conservation biotechnology, monitoring, and adaptive governance. The current crisis of biodiversity loss affects a million species, threatening their extinction, while plant genetic diversity is also disappearing at an alarming rate. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Third Report on the State of the World’s Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, 42% of the plant genetic resources evaluated for taxonomic diversity were no longer present in at least one country. papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Utilization of Nuclear Technology in Supply Chains: A Review of the Literature
papers.authors: Yohanes Dicka Parama, Andri Hermawan
papers.abstract: Background. Nuclear technology has strategic potential to enhance the safety, quality, traceability, and resilience of modern supply chains. However, existing studies remain fragmented across industrial sectors, highlighting the need for an integrative synthesis of its contributions to supply chain management. Aims. This study aims to identify, classify, and analyze nuclear technology applications across supply chain activities, focusing on their potential benefits, implementation challenges, and relevance to Indonesia. Methods. We conducted a narrative literature review using a targeted literature search and thematic synthesis of scientific publications and reports from national and international institutions published between 2014 and 2025. Result. The findings identify six major application domains: (1) food irradiation to improve food safety and extend product shelf life; (2) isotope analysis for product traceability and authenticity verification; (3) radioisotope tracers for industrial process monitoring and energy supply chains; (4) non-destructive testing to maintain logistics infrastructure integrity; (5) radiation sterilization in pharmaceutical and healthcare supply chain

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding where and how far animals move across broad ecological contexts is essential for guiding management decisions in natural resource and animal disease management. Commonly, applications predict movement metrics over spatial extents within existing geolocation datasets, which challenges their utility for landscape-scale management applications. Methods We collated geolocation data from 564 wild pigs spanning 25 studies across 10 states in the United States (U.S.). We summarized the distribution of displacement distances for each wild pig at two scales (net displacement, distance relative to an initial geolocation of residency over three months; daily displacement, distance between day-to-day shifts in where individuals geolocate) in each of four seasons. We fit gamma distributions to the individual-level displacement distributions and derived their mean and dispersion parameters as metrics of displacement magnitude and variation. papers.authors: Md Masud Rana, Md. Redwanur Rahman, Ameilia Zuliyanti Siregar
papers.abstract: In Bangladesh, rich agro-biodiversity is increasingly threatened by unsustainable pest management practices, environmental degradation, pest resistance, decline of beneficial species, and contamination of food and water. This study evaluates prevailing pest management strategies, their ecological and economic impacts, and opportunities to develop biodiversity- and eco-friendly pest control systems. A cross-sectional mixed-methods approach was applied across five agroecological zones, involving surveys of 500 smallholder farmers, 30 key informant interviews, ecological field assessments, and laboratory analysis of pesticide residues in soil, water, and vegetables. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially, while biodiversity indices measured species richness; qualitative data were thematically analyzed to explore knowledge, institutional barriers, and perceptions. Results show that 87% of farmers rely solely on chemical pesticides, often applying high doses based on visual inspection rather than integrated thresholds. papers.title: Strengthening coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) genebanks for a climate-resilient and sustainable future
papers.authors: Shunmugiah Veluchamy Ramesh, Vittal Niral, Kukkehalli Balachandra Hebbar
papers.abstract: Abstract Coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) is a multipurpose crop that supports millions of livelihoods across tropical regions, yet its genetic resources are increasingly threatened by climate change, emerging pests and diseases and changing production demands. Effective conservation of coconut genetic diversity is therefore essential for ensuring future breeding, climate resilience and sustainable production. This critical review evaluates recent advances in coconut genetic resource conservation, genebank management and emerging technologies supporting germplasm utilization. It examines the current status of global coconut genebanks coordinated through the International Coconut Genetic Resources Network, highlighting the strengths and limitations of existing conservation strategies, including field genebanks, in vitro conservation and cryopreservation. Recent developments in molecular characterization, genomics, artificial intelligence, digital technologies and tissue culture have substantially enhanced germplasm characterization, conservation efficiency and climate-resilient breeding. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: Sushila Bhattacharya, Lisa Fischer, Evrim Fer, Jennifer Snoozy, Grace N. Hagedorn
papers.abstract: Disruptions in purine metabolism contribute to a range of human diseases, from rare genetic disorders such as Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and xanthinuria to common conditions including gout and cancer. To better understand the metabolic networks that regulate purine homeostasis, we developed a Caenorhabditis elegans model of xanthine dehydrogenase ( xdh-1 ) deficiency. Remarkably, xdh-1 mutant animals form rare xanthine stones, recapitulating a hallmark of human xanthinuria. To uncover genetic regulators of purine homeostasis, we performed a forward genetic screen for mutations that exacerbate xanthine stone formation in xdh-1 mutants. This approach identified multiple loss-of-function alleles in a previously uncharacterized gene, which we named gda-1 . We show that gda-1 encodes an intestinal guanine deaminase that mediates a key enzymatic step in purine catabolism. The C. elegans genome also encodes a paralog, gda-2 , which shares guanine deaminase activity but is expressed in distinct tissues. papers.title: Global biodiversity models exhibit low predictive accuracy on local scales
papers.authors: Jakob Nyström, Jeffrey R. Smith, Lisa Mandle, Andrew Gonzalez, Thomas B. Schön
papers.abstract: Abstract Amid the global biodiversity crisis, there is high demand for spatially explicit biodiversity indicators. Global models that quantify human impacts on biodiversity provide important insights for conservation, but systematic testing of predictive performance has been lacking. Here, when evaluating alpha- and beta-diversity models using representative global data, we find that, despite land-use impacts in line with previous research, there is a challenging gap between effect size inference and local prediction. The results show that mixed models with study attributes as random effects, common in biodiversity meta-analysis and indicators, exhibit low predictive accuracy, driven by reliance on highly averaged fixed effects. Ecologically structured models that replace study random effects with biome, realm and taxonomic parameters show improved but still modest results in sampled contexts. Further, performance when extending predictions to other contexts remains low, related to distribution shifts in environmental conditions and biodiversity responses. These isolates demonstrated remarkable phenotypic plasticity, maintaining biofilm formation across varying pH, temperature and salinity levels. To maximize microbial stability and metabolic efficiency, sugarcane bagasse was utilized as a support matrix. papers.authors: , Azam Mahdipour, Mojgan Zaeimdar, , Mohammad Sadegh Sekhavatjou
papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: This study aimed to investigate the concentrations of heavy metals bound to airborne Particulate Matter (PM) in high-traffic districts of Tehran, Iran, and to determine the carcinogenic risk and Hazard Quotient (HQ) of these metals using a descriptive-applied method. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). After extracting the metals from fiberglass filters by acid digestion based on the ASTM (the American Society for Testing and Materials method), the concentrations of heavy metals were determined by an Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) device. Oxylipins are important regulators of insect immunity, in which eicosanoids generally promote antiviral responses whereas C18 epoxyoctadecamonoenoic acids (EpOMEs) act as immune suppressors. Although manipulation of insect immunity by plant viruses has been increasingly recognized, the molecular mechanisms by which TYLCV reshapes vector physiology to establish a permissive infection state remain poorly understood. Methodology TYLCV infection and localization in B. tabaci were analyzed using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), immunofluorescence assays (IFA), and quantitative PCR. Oxylipin functions were examined through oral delivery of prostaglandins, EpOMEs, pathway inhibitors, and lipid analogs. EpOME levels were quantified by LC–MS/MS. papers.abstract: Introduction Next-generation biotics are redefining microbiota-targeted strategies by combining beneficial microorganisms with bioactive plant-derived substrates. Pomegranate ( Punica granatum L.) leaves, an abundant agri-food by-product, represent a sustainable source of polyphenols with antioxidant, antimicrobial, and potential prebiotic and microbiota-modulating properties. This exploratory in vitro proof-of-concept study aimed to preliminarily characterize a pomegranate leaf extract (PLE), assess its antibacterial activity, evaluate its association with Saccharomyces boulardii growth and viability, and characterize the resulting yeast-derived fractions and heat-inactivated biomass. Methods A pomegranate leaf extract (PLE) was obtained by microwave-assisted extraction using a hydroethanolic solvent. PLE was preliminarily characterized using Folin–Ciocalteu, aluminum chloride, DPPH, and FTIR analyses. papers.authors: Fritjof Lammers, Valentina Peona, Reto Burri
papers.abstract: Abstract Contrary to long-held views, the exchange of genetic diversity between species by hybridization is now recognized as an important process contributing to the evolution of biodiversity. However, hybridization has molecular consequences beyond the exchange of genetic variation. The clash of divergent genomes upon hybridization can escalate genetic conflicts previously resolved in parental species—notably between transposable elements (TEs) and their repressors—and may unleash a cascade of molecular events inducing the evolution of chromosomal rearrangements (structural variants, SVs). Novel TE insertions and other SVs are often associated with cancer, reduced longevity, and genomic disorders, and usually inflict high fitness costs, thus they likely incur major constraints to gene flow among species and may constitute an integral component of reproductive isolation. Furthermore, in the presence of gene flow, certain SVs (e.g., inversions) may help protect beneficial combinations of alleles across genes from breaking up. papers.title: Handbook of the Anthropology of Mobilities
papers.authors: Natalia Bloch
papers.abstract: Things are constantly moving; animals, plants, objects, capital, businesses, services, diseases, media, images, information and ideas have mobilities that are dynamic and complex. The Anthropological Handbook of Mobility takes stock of the dispersed body of anthropological work on mobilities, as both an object of study and an analytical lens. From an anthropological point of view, this guide provides a comprehensive and accessible introduction to mobility studies for students, scholars, and anyone else wanting to know more about the implications of mobility.

papers.abstract: Abstract Filamentous fungi are ubiquitous in aquatic and aquaculture environments and may be relevant to fish health and food safety. However, information on culturable filamentous fungi recoverable from apparently healthy Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) in Egyptian aquaculture systems remains limited. This study investigated the genus-level composition, organ-associated distribution, and morphological characteristics of culturable filamentous fungi recovered from apparently healthy O. niloticus collected from commercial fish farms in Kafrelsheikh Governorate, Egypt. A total of 210 apparently healthy fish were sampled from 11 commercial farms. papers.abstract: Abstract Background & Objectives : Mosquitoes transmit serious human diseases, causing millions of deaths every year. The development of resistance to chemical insecticides has resulted in rebounding vectorial capacity, meaning that plants may serve as viable alternative sources of mosquito control agents. The present study critically tested the larvicidal activities of four candidate medicinal plant species: Ocimum forskolei , Gymnema sylvestre , Lippia javanica, and Datura stramonium . These species are traditionally used for mosquito control and are reported to be effective against larvae of mosquito vectors of malaria and arboviral diseases in Ethiopia. The extracts were evaluated against late third to early fourth instar larvae of Anopheles arabiensis, Anopheles stephensi , and Aedes aegypti. papers.title: Forces at the scale of the cell
papers.authors: Vijaykumar Krishnamurthy, Mandar M. Inamdar, Pramod A. Pullarkat, Gautam I. Menon
papers.source: OpenAlex / Reports on Progress in Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract The importance of molecular-scale forces in sculpting biological form and function has been acknowledged for more than a century. Accounting for forces in biology is a problem that lies at the intersection of soft condensed matter physics, statistical mechanics, and experimental methods, all adapted to a cellular context. This review surveys how forces arise within the cell. We provide a summary of the relevant background in cell biophysics, of soft-matter systems in and out of thermodynamic equilibrium, and of various force measurement methods. These ideas are then deployed to describe how forces are generated, transmitted, and sensed in specific cell-scale processes. We emphasize active matter descriptions, methodological tools that provide ways of incorporating non-equilibrium effects in a systematic manner into conceptual as well as quantitative descriptions. papers.title: Engineering Delivery across Plant Barriers: Nano- and Microtechnologies for Plant Bioengineering
papers.authors: Pisrut Phummirat, Andy Kah Ping Tay
papers.source: OpenAlex / ACS Bio & Med Chem Au
papers.abstract: Abstract Plant bioengineering is moving from proof-of-concept genetic modification toward programmable, spatially controlled, and environmentally responsive intervention in living plants. Yet delivery remains the central bottleneck. Plant tissues impose a nested series of barriers, including the cuticle, stomata, trichomes, cell wall, plasma membrane, apoplast, vascular network, organelle membranes, and rhizosphere microbiome, that restrict the transport and functional deployment of nucleic acids, proteins, sensors, agrochemicals, and living microbes. Conventional approaches such as Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, biolistics, viral vectors, foliar spraying, soil drenching, and trunk injections remain valuable, but they are often limited by genotype dependence, tissue damage, low spatial precision, poor environmental stability, or weak translation across plant species and developmental stages. Nano- and microdelivery technologies offer a delivery-science framework for overcoming these constraints. papers.title: Rapid environmental DNA detection with isothermal amplification methods: a comparison with the real-time quantitative PCR in the natterjack toad (Epidalea calamita).
papers.authors: Chieux Abigael, Alessia Guerrieri, Eva Bellemain, Frédéric Boyer, Thomas Merzi
papers.abstract: Species detection relying on environmental DNA (eDNA) traditionally relies on Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR). This amplification technique takes in general a minimum of one hour and requires in most cases access to specialized laboratories and equipment. Isothermal amplification techniques, originating from clinical research, are emerging as rapid and field-deployable alternative methods. Yet, whether their sensitivity, specificity, and cost/time-efficiency are comparable to the traditional real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) remains to be assessed. In this work, we compare the performance of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with qPCR to detect the natterjack toad (Epidalea calamita) from aquatic filtrations. This objective was achieved in three steps. First, we developed LAMP and RPA primers specific to the target species based on its mitochondrial genome. Second, we amplified DNA extracts from E. calamita and from tissues of closely related species using real-time fluorescence detection with LAMP, RPA, and qPCR commercially available protocols to evaluate and compare the sensitivity and specificity of the three methods. papers.title: Organic Amendments for Simultaneous Soil Carbon Sequestration and Soil-Borne Pathogen Suppression: Mechanisms and Perspectives
papers.authors: Qudrat Ullah, Esha Arshad, Kainat Fatima, Waqas Haider, Muhammad Qasim
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
papers.abstract: The depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the escalating prevalence of soil-borne plant pathogens represent critical challenges to terrestrial biogeochemical stability and global food security. With approximately 24% of terrestrial carbon reserves lost and over US$220 billion in annual crop losses attributed to soil-borne diseases, understanding biotic and geochemical controls on soil health is essential. This review evaluates the dual functionality of organic amendments (agricultural residues, animal manures, and urban biosolids) as drivers of simultaneous carbon restoration and pathogen suppression. We analyze the mechanisms governing these benefits, focusing on the biogeochemical coupling of element cycles and microbiome-mediated processes such as the formation of recalcitrant carbon, organo-mineral protection, and microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE). Biochar applications can increase SOC stocks by 26–33% (11.5–14.6 Mg ha⁻¹), while silicon-modified biochar reduces the bacterial wilt index caused by Ralstonia solanacearum by 73.4%. Furthermore, we examine the geochemical mechanisms of pathogen suppression through antibiosis, resource competition, and signaling disruption.

Methods This study characterized bacterial communities in five compartments of Pinus massoniana (needles, stems, roots, rhizosphere soil and bulk soil) across four stages of pine wilt disease (PWD; healthy, early, intermediate and late) using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and functional prediction. Results The results showed that bacterial community dynamics were significantly influenced by compartment and disease stage. Notably, the stem compartment exhibited substantial changes: Chao1 index significantly increased at the intermediate stage, whereas Chao1, Shannon and Shannoneven indices declined at late stage. Also in stem compartment, the late stage was characterized by marked enrichment of the phylum Proteobacteria, accompanied by elevated relative abundances of the genera Pseudomonas and Methylobacterium .
